Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The building opens at 9:30, so the band has half an hour to carry in equipment and get settled before the reserved time begins. The booking includes the room, a basic drum kit, two vocal microphones, and use of the shared loading area.

Mara made the reservation for four people: herself on drums, Leon Price on bass, Tessa Ward on guitar, and Niko Bell on vocals and guitar. The band is called Juniper Static. They are preparing six songs for a small neighborhood arts fundraiser the following weekend, but the rehearsal is not a performance and no audience is expected. The room is booked for a full three hours because they need time to check the kit, work through transitions, and record a few reference takes. They have not arranged an engineer, and the building’s staff will not operate recording equipment for them.

The standard kit has a five-piece shell set, one crash cymbal, one ride cymbal, a hi-hat, a throne, and a single kick pedal. Mara asked whether she could bring her own snare and double pedal; the booking notes say that personal hardware is permitted as long as it is removed before the end of the session. The house kit is shared, so the band should not adjust the rack clamps with tools or move the bass drum away from the marked mat. A pair of sticks is not included. Mara plans to bring her own sticks, snare, pedal, and a small roll of gaffer tape for securing cables.

The arrival plan depends on the loading area. If the ferry terminal’s side gate is open when they arrive, Leon will unload the bass amp and guitar cases there, then move the van to the public parking lot on Alder Street. If the gate is locked, the group will use the front entrance and carry everything up the stairs in two trips. The loading area is shared with a pottery class that ends at 10:00, so the band has been asked not to block the marked walkway or leave cases beside the fire door. Tessa has the van, while Niko is bringing a compact vocal amplifier and two instrument stands by bicycle.

Mara called the booking desk on Tuesday to ask about the room’s recording setup. The staff member said, “There is a stereo recorder on the shelf, but please bring an SD card; the room does not supply one.” Mara added an SD card to the equipment list and will check that it has enough space before leaving home. The recorder takes a standard 3.5-millimeter stereo input, but the group intends to use its built-in microphones rather than connect instruments directly. They want rough reference recordings, not a polished demo, and they will listen back through the small monitor speakers during the session.

The booking includes a 10-minute sound check at the start, but that time is part of the three-hour reservation. The band has divided the rehearsal into blocks so they do not spend the whole morning tuning and talking. They will begin with “North Window,” “Paper Maps,” and “Cinder Track,” then take a short water break. After that, they will work on the ending of “Small Hours,” whose last chorus has been coming in too early, and run “Low Bridge” at two tempos. The final half hour is reserved for “Orchard Lights” and a complete run-through of the six-song set in performance order.

1. Room and arrival details
   - Reservation: Saturday, May 18, 10:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.
   - Location: Harbor Room, second floor of the old ferry terminal, Alder Street.
   - Building access: from 9:30 a.m.; use the blue door marked Studio B.
   - Booking contact: Mara Chen; confirmation number HR-518-104.
   - Parking: public spaces on Alder Street; do not leave the van in the loading area.
   - Included equipment: basic drum kit, two vocal microphones, and shared loading access.

The room has a wall clock, two music stands, and a small table beside the recorder. The band is bringing its own cables, water bottles, tuner, and extension cord. Drinks must stay on the table or on the floor away from the kit, and food is not allowed in Studio B. The terminal has a water fountain by the ground-floor restrooms, but there is no café inside the building. Niko will bring four refillable bottles, and Leon has offered to bring earplugs for anyone who needs them. The group has agreed to keep the door closed during songs because another room is used for piano lessons on Saturday mornings.

The booking desk also explained the cancellation and late-arrival rules. A cancellation made at least 48 hours before the reservation can be moved to another available date, while a later cancellation is charged at the full room rate. If the band arrives after 10:15, the reserved end time remains 1:00 p.m.; staff cannot extend the session if another booking follows. Mara has put the desk number in the group chat, but nobody has called to change or cancel the reservation. The band plans to meet outside the front entrance at 9:35, check that everyone has arrived, and carry the equipment upstairs together.

After the rehearsal, the band will pack personal equipment first, return the house cymbals and microphones to their marked places, and leave the kit on its mat. They must be out of the room by 1:00, including the time needed to carry cases back downstairs. Mara will make a brief note of which reference takes need to be shared, but the group has not decided whether to send the recordings to the fundraiser organizer. If the side gate is still open when they leave, Tessa will bring the van around for loading; otherwise, they will carry the cases to the public parking lot.
